latest_news.headline: Yemen campaign revision: government claims Mokha recapture and new Marib advances; control unverified
latest_news.text: Editorial revision of the retained campaign. Full original Saba military and prime-minister accounts and full Al Arabiya report read. The new detail is the government claim to Mokha and specified Marib advances, not independent confirmation of a control change. Earlier Dhubab reports and the Houthi denial remain retained. All claims originate with the same government-side chain; no casualty totals are adopted. Saba date/time lacks a timezone, and its displayed chronology across related releases is inconsistent, so no exact publication or battlefield instant is invented.

latest_news.implication: Government-side reporting adds claimed coastal and Marib gains; actual territorial control, port operation and casualty totals remain unverified.
latest_news.next_trigger: The prime minister directs restoration of services and state institutions in Mokha; no completion date is given.
latest_news.material_revision: Government-side reports now claim Mokha recapture and specified Marib advances beyond the earlier offensive announcement.

latest_news.headline: Newly reviewed UKMTO 152-26: tanker master reports turning back after IRGC threat near Khasab
latest_news.text: Original advisory 152-26 says a tanker inbound through Hormuz was hailed by the IRGC and told to turn back or be targeted. The master confirmed compliance. UKMTO records a report at 08:27 UTC October 5, 11 nautical miles north of Khasab, Oman, and says authorities are investigating. This newly reviewed October 5 notice is distinct from retained October 2-3 incidents. Its publication instant is unknown. UKMTO relays a master report; Khaleej Times repeats the same notice. No independent radio authentication, attribution or vessel-track verification.
latest_news.originating_source: UK Maritime Trade Operations original master-sourced product
latest_news.implication: The master reports a threatened tanker transit was reversed; the notice does not report a strike, injury or verified identity of the vessel.
latest_news.next_trigger: UKMTO says authorities are investigating; findings remain pending.

latest_news.text: Original warning 156-26 records an incident at 16:37 UTC October 5 in Hormuz. A tanker master reports an unknown projectile strike and an engine-room fire being fought by the crew. This newly reviewed October 5 notice is distinct from retained October 2-3 incidents. Its publication instant is unknown. One original UKMTO warning relays a master report. No independent physical verification or separate reputable report of this particular warning obtained.

latest_news.implication: A tanker strike and engine-room fire are reported by its master; attribution, damage extent and subsequent crew or environmental status remain unverified.

latest_news.headline: Yemen campaign revision: spokesman announces Sanaa offensive; coalition claims direct air support
latest_news.text: An editorial revision of the existing campaign, not a newly invented campaign or source-issued correction. Saba 153488 quotes Majed al-Nazili announcing the start of a strategic attack on Sanaa using modern capabilities. Saba 153480 quotes coalition spokesman Turki al-Malki claiming direct fighter participation and continuing air support for government forces and protection of Bab al-Mandab. Saba 153476 names the existing operation Dawn of Yemen and explicitly refers back to the Sunday start announcement. Naming alone is not counted as material; the additional Sanaa attack and direct coalition participation claims are the supported revisions. Aircraft and target-destruction totals remain belligerent claims and are not adopted. None of the same-side statements independently verifies execution, damage, strait security or territorial control. Publication displays are October 5 at 10:09, 09:18 and 08:23 without a timezone; exact publication instants are unknown.

latest_news.headline: Khurais revision: AFP reports pipeline damage and stoppage; Reuters and Bloomberg report uninterrupted oil flow
latest_news.text: The retained October 4 Houthi statement naming Aramco in Khurais was reread from exact Telegram post 3802. Newly reviewed October 5 CBS/AFP reporting quotes an unnamed Saudi energy-sector source alleging a Sunday strike on a Khurais pumping station, major damage and a renewed East-West pipeline stoppage. The same report records a conflicting Reuters source account that oil remained flowing. A full Dawn Reuters-attributed dispatch says flows have not been interrupted, while available Bloomberg reporting describes normal flow based on unnamed people familiar with the matter. This updates the prior target claim with a contested infrastructure/operational-impact account, not an authenticated strike or confirmed shutdown. The anonymous sources cannot be established as independent of each other or of the parties. Responsibility, exact damage, the event instant and measured throughput remain unverified. The CBS pipeline-entry publication timestamp is 11:28 UTC on October 5, distinct from the underlying October 4 statement and collection/review times. This is the same retained Khurais incident, not another attack; the separate Riyadh-fire incident is unchanged.
latest_news.sources: Exact original Houthi post, full CBS/AFP live entry, full short Dawn Reuters-attributed dispatch and available Bloomberg text read; anonymous and contradictory claims remain unverified.
latest_news.originating_source: CBS/AFP unnamed Saudi energy-sector source; Reuters and Bloomberg report contrary oil-flow accounts
latest_news.implication: New reporting concerns the East-West oil export route, but conflicting flow accounts do not establish a pipeline shutdown or quantify lost exports.
latest_news.next_trigger: Public context unavailable; consult the original source.
latest_news.material_revision: A new AFP damage/stoppage account is contradicted by Reuters and Bloomberg reports of continuing flow.

latest_news.headline: ISW and Yemeni sources report Houthi entry into Al-Turbah and pressure on Taiz-Aden supply routes
latest_news.text: ISW's October 4 assessment describes Houthi advances into Al-Turbah and along the Taiz-Aden supply network, citing claimed geolocated imagery and original Yemeni-source interviews published by Sky News Arabia. Sky News Arabia says sources reported Houthi entry into Al-Turbah and continuing government fighting near the road. The analyst post identifies an Al-Shamatin police-station location, but the underlying video and geolocation were not independently authenticated in this review. The new town-entry report is distinct from the retained October 1 IED disruption. Whole-town control, enduring closure, casualty totals and capture of Taiz City are not established by this review. ISW separately says it had not yet observed offensive operations following the government's announcement; this does not prove no operations occurred.
latest_news.sources: Full ISW assessment and original Sky News Arabia source interviews read. ISW cites these interviews and analyst posts; different hosts are not independent confirmation of control.
latest_news.originating_source: ISW/CTP October 4 assessment, with original Sky News Arabia Yemeni-source interviews and a geolocation analyst post
latest_news.implication: Reported gains threaten Taiz's reinforcement and resupply routes; control and lasting road closure are not independently verified.
latest_news.next_trigger: Public context unavailable; consult the original source.

latest_news.headline: Yemen campaign revision: Al-Alimi announces military operations to retake Houthi-held territory
latest_news.text: Saba publishes the full October 4 presidential statement announcing the start of military operations to retake remaining territory and directions for armed forces to begin assigned missions. A separate original military spokesman statement announces implementation. Reuters, CNN and BBC report the same announcement. This updates the retained campaign-planning incident, not a second campaign or proof of a new battlefield phase. BBC says it is not yet clear whether this represents a new phase. No territorial gain, casualty total, Saudi operational participation or independently verified ground launch is established. The primary displayed publication has no timezone; its instant remains unknown. No independent-verification or urgent qualification.
latest_news.sources: Original Saba statements read in full; Reuters syndication, CNN and BBC report the same statement, not independent battlefield verification.
latest_news.originating_source: Yemen government Saba: full presidential and military statements
latest_news.implication: A presidential start announcement supersedes planning-only status; the campaign’s implementation and territorial effects remain unverified.
latest_news.next_trigger: Public context unavailable; consult the original source.
latest_news.material_revision: Previously reported campaign planning now has an explicit presidential start announcement; implementation remains unverified.

latest_news.headline: Mekelle revision: AFP journalist reports federal patrols and key-institution presence; full control remains attributed
latest_news.text: AFP’s October 4 original report says a local journalist described federal troops patrolling Mekelle and manning key institutions, with communications restored. A pro-government militia commander separately told AFP his forces had taken control. Resident accounts describe closed shops and absent police. These are additions to the retained withdrawal, entry and airport-control reports, not another capture event. Whole-city control, precise transfer time and end of fighting remain unverified. The regional summit is still described as scheduled, not a verified final outcome. Conflicting original publication/modification metadata are retained privately; exact publication instant is left unknown. No independent-verification upgrade or urgent qualification.
latest_news.sources: AFP’s original interviews read in full; attributed reports, without independent whole-city control verification.
latest_news.originating_source: AFP original journalist, resident and pro-government militia interviews
latest_news.implication: AFP’s journalist account extends reported federal presence beyond the airport; whole-city control remains attributed and unverified.
latest_news.next_trigger: Public context unavailable; consult the original source.
latest_news.material_revision: October 4 AFP journalist account adds patrols and key-institution presence to earlier airport and entry reports.

latest_news.headline: Houthis name Khurais as an additional Aramco target in an October 4 strike claim; success unverified
latest_news.text: The original Houthi spokesman's English Telegram statement names Khurais, alongside Riyadh, as a target of claimed ballistic-missile and drone operations. The exact post 3802 has an October 4 13:00:52 UTC publication timestamp. ISW discusses the same statement and an analyst's reported fire near a Khurais pumping station. Neither publication independently establishes weapon impact, the fire's cause, facility damage, operational disruption or responsibility. The analyst's attribution is expressly tentative. Khurais is a separately named claimed target; the repeat Riyadh component is not counted as a newly verified October 4 strike or a revision of the existing October 3 fire. Claimed Saudi strike totals and interception performance are not adopted as facts.
latest_news.sources: Original spokesman statement read with exact post metadata; ISW and analyst attribution read but not independently verified.
latest_news.originating_source: Houthi military spokesman original English Telegram statement 3802
latest_news.implication: Khurais is an additional claimed Saudi oil target; strike success, fire causation and operational impact remain unverified.
latest_news.next_trigger: Public context unavailable; consult the original source.

latest_news.headline: PCG allegation: Chinese coast guard blocked anti-blast-fishing pursuit near Thitu
latest_news.sources: BusinessWorld original reporting and Reuters syndicated by Straits Times share the PCG allegation, not independent incident confirmation. Distinct from retained Jia Hai Ke 7 monitoring near Batanes.
latest_news.originating_source: BusinessWorld / Pexcel John Bacon
latest_news.implication: PCG says a civilian law-enforcement pursuit was obstructed and abandoned for safety; no casualties or combat are established, and the claim remains unverified.
latest_news.next_trigger: Tarriela says the incident will be documented and referred to the Philippine Department of Foreign Affairs; no action date is supplied.

latest_news.headline: Newly reviewed UKMTO Warning 150-26: tanker master reports a projectile hit and engine-room damage; incident date unknown
latest_news.sources: Full original UKMTO notice; Arab Times repeats the same master report. Warning report date and time are explicitly TBC; exact issuance time unknown.
latest_news.originating_source: United Kingdom Maritime Trade Operations
latest_news.implication: The tanker master reports engine-room damage, with crew safe and no environmental impact reported; vessel identity, attack time and responsibility remain unknown.
latest_news.next_trigger: UKMTO says authorities are investigating; findings are not supplied by this notice.
